thread:
devin: Heads-up — canaries started spiking compile-queue and KV evictions after today's runtime roll.
ci-bot: PERF ALERT: compile_queue_time increased +42% vs baseline for service/model-serving (see dashboard https://dash.redwood/api/serving/compile). Incident ID: PERF-2360
maya: I'm seeing a compile storm on p3 pools, lots of kernel JIT jobs. KV cache thrashing (evictions up ~3.1x).
li: stack-trace from agent on one host:
```
[WARN] compile_queue: 312 jobs backlog
[INFO] kernel_selector: selected variant x64_fp16_q4 (seed=0x9f) -> compile triggered
[kv-cache] eviction_rate=0.52 per sec
```
ryan: rough timeline matches merge PR #4521 (kernel-policy: prefer-hot-path heuristic) merged ~8m before alert. @jordan you landed that right?
jordan: yeah that was mine. It changed the scoring to bias hotpath heuristics and to eagerly compile candidate kernels for short batches.
anjali: can we bisect quickly? ci-bot, can you point to exact commit range that got promoted to canary?
ci-bot: Promotion job 2026-03-17T16:18 promoted commit 4a1b2c3 -> 6f2d9aa into canary group.
devin: quick repro on staging: run small-batch workload (batch_size=1, seq=64) repeatedly, compile queue floods after ~2000 requests. Repro script:
```
for i in $(seq 1 3000); do curl -sS -X POST https://staging.api.redwood/generate -d '{"model":"rwd-7b","input":"hi"}' >/dev/null; done
```
maya: heap of compile logs show selector preferred kernel A over B despite lower latency in previous perf runs. Looks like selection score used compile_cost estimate incorrectly (multiplied by weight 10 by default).
li: found suspect line in new heuristic: `score -= compile_cost * 10` should have been `score -= compile_cost * 0.1` — that would explain eager compile bias.
ryan: if that's true it explains both compile churn and KV churn (worse exec variance causes more cache fragmentation).
devin: mitigation options: 1) revert PR #4521 in canary 2) flip runtime flag `KERNEL_POLICY_STRICT=0` to disable new scoring 3) throttle compile concurrency to 4.
anjali: can we flip feature flag first as lowest blast radius? How to flip config for canary only?
ops-bot: To change canary config: `redwoodctl rollout set-flag --group=canary --flag=KERNEL_POLICY_STRICT --value=false` (takes ~30s to propagate)
jordan: I'll prepare a hotfix PR to change the multiplier to 0.1 and push a config rollback if needed.
maya: test: after setting flag to false on canary, compile queue drops to ~40 jobs and eviction rate normalizes. Can confirm on two canary hosts.
ci-bot: CANARY METRICS: compile_queue_time returned to baseline within 6m of flag flip.
devin: good. Plan: keep flag off for 2h, run extended canary, then either merge hotfix or revert if regression persists. Assignments: @jordan hotfix PR, @li run deeper perf run with longer sequences, @maya watch canary metrics and prepare rollback playbook.
ryan: also add a unit test for scoring math — ints vs floats bug is nasty.
jordan: PR opened: https://git.redwood/r/4521-hotfix (patch changes multiplier to 0.1 and adds test). Will request review now.
devin: thanks all. If we see any second wave, revert rollout and open incident. For now keeping this thread updated.
